sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity uktaḥ sa tadā tena tulādhāreṇa dhīmatā provāca vacanaṃ dhīmāñ jājalir japatāṃ varaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Addressed thus by the wise Tulādhāra, the sagacious Jājali, foremost among those who murmur prayers, then spoke these words.

sanskrit: vikrīṇānaḥ sarvarasān sarvagandhāṃś ca vāṇija vanaspatīn oṣadhīś ca teṣāṃ mūlaphalāni ca
english: O trader, you who sell all manner of flavors and all manner of fragrances, and trees and herbs, and their roots and fruits as well—

sanskrit: adhyagā naiṣṭhikīṃ buddhiṃ kutas tvām idam āgatam etad ācakṣva me sarvaṃ nikhilena mahāmate
english: how have you attained this conclusive wisdom? Whence has it come to you? Tell me all of it, entire and without omission, O greatly intelligent one.

sanskrit: evam uktas tulādhāro brāhmaṇena yaśasvinā uvāca dharmasūkṣmāṇi vaiśyo dharmārthatattvavit jājaliṃ kaṣṭatapasaṃ jñānatṛptas tadā nṛpa
english: Thus addressed by the illustrious brāhmaṇa, Tulādhāra the vaiśya, knower of the truths of dharma and its purpose, then spoke of the subtleties of dharma to Jājali of severe austerities, himself contented in wisdom, O king.

sanskrit: vedāhaṃ jājale dharmaṃ sarahasyaṃ sanātanam sarvabhūtahitaṃ maitraṃ purāṇaṃ yaṃ janā viduḥ
english: I know, O Jājali, the eternal dharma with its secret—the ancient dharma of goodwill, conducing to the welfare of all beings, which people have known of old.

sanskrit: adroheṇaiva bhūtānām alpadroheṇa vā punaḥ yā vṛttiḥ sa paro dharmas tena jīvāmi jājale
english: That mode of life which works no injury to creatures, or but little injury—that is the highest dharma, and by it I live, O Jājali.

sanskrit: paricchinnaiḥ kāṣṭhatṛṇair mayedaṃ śaraṇaṃ kṛtam alaktaṃ padmakaṃ tuṅgaṃ gandhāṃś coccāvacāṃs tathā
english: With sticks and grasses already cut by others I have made this dwelling of mine; lac, the lotus-perfume, costly aloe-wood, and fragrances both high and low—

sanskrit: rasāṃś ca tāṃs tān viprarṣe madyavarjān ahaṃ bahūn krītvā vai prativikrīṇe parahastād amāyayā
english: and these and those many flavors, save intoxicants, O sage among brāhmaṇas—having bought them from another's hand, I sell them again without any deceit.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ yaḥ suhṛn nityaṃ sarveṣāṃ ca hite rataḥ karmaṇā manasā vācā sa dharmaṃ veda jājale
english: He who is ever a friend to all, and devoted to the welfare of all in deed, in thought, and in word—he knows dharma, O Jājali.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ pareṣāṃ karmāṇi praśaṃsāmi śapāmi vā ākāśasyeva viprarṣe paśyaṃl lokasya citratām
english: I neither praise nor condemn the deeds of others, beholding the manifold variety of the world as one beholds the sky, O sage among brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: nānurudhye virudhye vā na dveṣmi na ca kāmaye samo 'smi sarvabhūteṣu paśya me jājale vratam
english: I neither favor nor oppose; I neither hate nor desire; I am the same toward all beings. Behold my vow, O Jājali.

sanskrit: iṣṭāniṣṭavimuktasya prītirāgabahiṣkṛtaḥ tulā me sarvabhūteṣu samā tiṣṭhati jājale
english: For one freed from the liked and the disliked, with fondness and passion cast out, my scale stands even toward all beings, O Jājali.

sanskrit: iti māṃ tvaṃ vijānīhi sarvalokasya jājale samaṃ matimatāṃ śreṣṭha samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanam
english: Know me then, O Jājali, to be impartial toward the whole world, O best of the wise—one to whom a clod, a stone, and gold are alike.

sanskrit: yathāndhabadhironmattā ucchvāsaparamāḥ sadā devair apihitadvārāḥ sopamā paśyato mama
english: As the blind, the deaf, and the maddened, having only their breath, are forever with their doors shut by the gods—such, in my seeing, is the likeness of men.

sanskrit: yathā vṛddhāturakṛśā niḥspṛhā viṣayān prati tathārthakāmabhogeṣu mamāpi vigatā spṛhā
english: As the old, the sick, and the wasted are without longing for sense-objects, so too has my own longing for wealth, desire, and enjoyments wholly passed away.

sanskrit: yadā cāyaṃ na bibheti yadā cāsmān na bibhyati yadā necchati na dveṣṭi tadā sidhyati vai dvijaḥ
english: When a man fears not, and when others fear not from him, when he neither desires nor hates—then indeed the twice-born is perfected.

sanskrit: yadā na kurute bhāvaṃ sarvabhūteṣu pāpakam karmaṇā manasā vācā brahma saṃpadyate tadā
english: When he harbors no evil intent toward any being, in deed, in thought, or in word—then he attains to Brahman.

sanskrit: na bhūto na bhaviṣyaś ca na ca dharmo 'sti kaś cana yo 'bhayaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ sa prāpnoty abhayaṃ padam
english: There has been, and there will be, no dharma whatever to equal it: he who is a refuge of safety to all beings attains the fearless state.

sanskrit: yasmād udvijate lokaḥ sarvo mṛtyumukhād iva vākkrūrād daṇḍapāruṣyāt sa prāpnoti mahad bhayam
english: But he from whom the whole world shrinks as from the very jaws of death—through cruelty of speech and harshness of punishment—he himself comes upon great fear.

sanskrit: yathāvad vartamānānāṃ vṛddhānāṃ putrapautriṇām anuvartāmahe vṛttam ahiṃsrāṇāṃ mahātmanām
english: We follow the conduct of the high-souled elders who lived rightly, blessed with sons and grandsons, who did no harm to any creature.

sanskrit: pranaṣṭaḥ śāśvato dharmaḥ sadācāreṇa mohitaḥ tena vaidyas tapasvī vā balavān vā vimohyate
english: The eternal dharma has been lost, obscured by what passes for good custom; by that custom the learned, the ascetic, or the mighty is led astray.

sanskrit: ācārāj jājale prājñaḥ kṣipraṃ dharmam avāpnuyāt evaṃ yaḥ sādhubhir dāntaś cared adrohacetasā
english: Through right conduct, O Jājali, the wise man would swiftly attain dharma—he who, self-restrained, moves among the good with a heart free of malice.

sanskrit: nadyāṃ yathā ceha kāṣṭham uhyamānaṃ yadṛcchayā yadṛcchayaiva kāṣṭhena saṃdhiṃ gaccheta kena cit
english: As a log of wood borne along by chance in a river might, by mere chance, come together with some other log—

sanskrit: tatrāparāṇi dārūṇi saṃsṛjyante tatas tataḥ tṛṇakāṣṭhakarīṣāṇi kadā cinn asamīkṣayā evam evāyam ācāraḥ prādurbhūto yatas tataḥ
english: and there yet other timbers join from this side and that—grasses, sticks, and dung, drifting at times unregarded—even so has this custom of men arisen, from this source and that.

sanskrit: yasmān nodvijate bhūtaṃ jātu kiṃ cit kathaṃ cana abhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyaḥ sa prāpnoti sadā mune
english: He from whom no creature ever shrinks at all, in any way, attains forever safety from all beings, O sage.

sanskrit: yasmād udvijate vidvan sarvaloko vṛkād iva krośatas tīram āsādya yathā sarve jalecarāḥ
english: But he from whom the whole world flees, O learned one, as from a wolf, as all water-creatures flee to the shore when one cries out aloud—

sanskrit: sahāyavān dravyavān yaḥ subhago 'nyo 'paras tathā tatas tān eva kavayaḥ śāstreṣu pravadanty uta kīrtyartham alpahṛllekhāḥ paṭavaḥ kṛtsnanirṇayāḥ
english: One has helpers, another has wealth, yet another is fortunate—it is of just such men that the poets speak in the treatises, clever men of shallow conscience and ready conclusions, all for the sake of fame.

sanskrit: tapobhir yajñadānaiś ca vākyaiḥ prajñāśritais tathā prāpnoty abhayadānasya yad yat phalam ihāśnute
english: Whatever fruit the gift of safety to all beings yields, that very fruit one enjoys here through austerities, through sacrifices and gifts, and through words rooted in wisdom.

sanskrit: loke yaḥ sarvabhūtebhyo dadāty abhayadakṣiṇām sa sarvayajñair ījānaḥ prāpnoty abhayadakṣiṇām na bhūtānām ahiṃsāyā jyāyān dharmo 'sti kaś cana
english: He who in this world gives to all beings the gift of safety as his sacrificial fee gains the reward of the gift of safety, as one who has offered every sacrifice; there is no dharma greater than non-violence toward living beings.

sanskrit: yasmān nodvijate bhūtaṃ jātu kiṃ cit kathaṃ cana so 'bhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyaḥ saṃprāpnoti mahāmune
english: He from whom no creature ever shrinks at all, in any way, attains complete safety from all beings, O great sage.

sanskrit: yasmād udvijate lokaḥ sarpād veśmagatād iva na sa dharmam avāpnoti iha loke paratra ca
english: But he from whom the world shrinks as from a serpent come into the house attains no dharma, neither in this world nor in the next.

sanskrit: sarvabhūtātmabhūtasya samyag bhūtāni paśyataḥ devāpi mārge muhyanti apadasya padaiṣiṇaḥ
english: For one who has made himself the self of all beings and beholds all creatures rightly, the gods themselves are bewildered as to his path, for he leaves no track, though they seek his footprint.

sanskrit: dānaṃ bhūtābhayasyāhuḥ sarvadānebhya uttamam bravīmi te satyam idaṃ śraddadhasva ca jājale
english: The gift of safety to living beings, they say, is the highest of all gifts. I tell you this in truth—believe it, O Jājali.

sanskrit: sa eva subhago bhūtvā punar bhavati durbhagaḥ vyāpattiṃ karmaṇāṃ dṛṣṭvā jugupsanti janāḥ sadā
english: The very man who was fortunate becomes wretched again; seeing the ruinous undoing of deeds, people ever turn away in revulsion.

sanskrit: akāraṇo hi nehāsti dharmaḥ sūkṣmo 'pi jājale bhūtabhavyārtham eveha dharmapravacanaṃ kṛtam
english: For no dharma here is without a reason, however subtle, O Jājali; it is for the sake of present and future beings that the teaching of dharma was set forth.

sanskrit: sūkṣmatvān na sa vijñātuṃ śakyate bahunihnavaḥ upalabhyāntarā cānyān ācārān avabudhyate
english: Because of its subtlety it cannot be fully grasped, having many a hidden turn; yet, perceiving it in part, one comes to understand the other customs as well.

sanskrit: ye ca chindanti vṛṣaṇān ye ca bhindanti nastakān vahanti mahato bhārān badhnanti damayanti ca
english: Those who cut off the testicles of beasts, those who pierce their nostrils, who load them with heavy burdens, who bind them and break them to the yoke—

sanskrit: hatvā sattvāni khādanti tān kathaṃ na vigarhase mānuṣā mānuṣān eva dāsabhogena buñjate
english: and who kill living creatures and devour them—how is it you do not censure these? Men make use of their fellow men, enjoying them as slaves;

sanskrit: vadhabandhavirodhena kārayanti divāniśam ātmanā cāpi jānāsi yad duḥkhaṃ vadhatāḍane
english: by killing, binding, and coercion they force them to labor day and night. You yourself know what pain there is in being struck and slain.

sanskrit: pañcendriyeṣu bhūteṣu sarvaṃ vasati daivatam ādityaś candramā vāyur brahmā prāṇaḥ kratur yamaḥ
english: In beings endowed with the five senses dwells all that is divine—Āditya, the moon, Vāyu, Brahmā, the breath of life, sacrifice, and Yama.

sanskrit: tāni jīvāni vikrīya kā mṛteṣu vicāraṇā kā taile kā ghṛte brahman madhuny apsv auṣadheṣu vā
english: When you traffic in these living things, what scruple is there over the dead? What scruple, O brāhmaṇa, over oil, over clarified butter, over honey, water, or herbs?

sanskrit: adaṃśamaśake deśe sukhaṃ saṃvardhitān paśūn tāṃś ca mātuḥ priyāñ jānann ākramya bahudhā narāḥ bahudaṃśakuśān deśān nayanti bahukardamān
english: Cattle reared in comfort in a land free of gadflies and mosquitoes—knowing them dear to their mothers—men seize and in many ways drive off to regions thick with gadflies and sharp grass and deep mire.

sanskrit: vāhasaṃpīḍitā dhuryāḥ sīdanty avidhināpare na manye bhrūṇahatyāpi viśiṣṭā tena karmaṇā
english: Draught-beasts crushed by their loads sink down, others undone against all rule. I do not think even the slaying of an embryo worse than that act.

sanskrit: kṛṣiṃ sādhv iti manyante sā ca vṛttiḥ sudāruṇā bhūmiṃ bhūmiśayāṃś caiva hanti kāṣṭham ayomukham tathaivānaḍuho yuktān samavekṣasva jājale
english: Men deem agriculture a virtuous calling, yet that livelihood is most cruel: the iron-mouthed plough wounds the earth and the creatures that lodge within it. And look likewise upon the oxen yoked to it, O Jājali.

sanskrit: aghnyā iti gavāṃ nāma ka enān hantum arhati mahac cakārākuśalaṃ pṛṣadhro gālabhann iva
english: 'Not to be slain'—such is the very name of cattle; who then has the right to slay them? Pṛṣadhra wrought a great evil, as one who slaughters a cow.

sanskrit: ṛṣayo yatayo hy etan nahuṣe pratyavedayan gāṃ mātaraṃ cāpy avadhīr vṛṣabhaṃ ca prajāpatim akāryaṃ nahuṣākārṣīr lapsyāmas tvatkṛte bhayam
english: For the seers and the ascetics declared this to Nahuṣa: 'You have slain the cow, who is a mother, and the bull, who is the Lord of Creatures; you have done, Nahuṣa, what ought not be done, and through you we shall meet with terror.'

sanskrit: śataṃ caikaṃ ca rogāṇāṃ sarvabhūteṣv apātayan ṛṣayas te mahābhāgāḥ prajāsv eva hi jājale bhrūṇahaṃ nahuṣaṃ tv āhur na te hoṣyāmahe haviḥ
english: And those greatly blessed seers brought down a hundred and one diseases upon all creatures, upon all living beings, O Jājali, and they pronounced Nahuṣa a slayer of the unborn, saying: 'We shall offer no oblation for you.'

sanskrit: ity uktvā te mahātmānaḥ sarve tattvārthadarśinaḥ ṛṣayo yatayaḥ śāntās tarasā pratyavedayan
english: Having spoken thus, those high-souled ones, all beholders of the true meaning—the seers and the tranquil ascetics—at once made their declaration.

sanskrit: īdṛśān aśivān ghorān ācārān iha jājale kevalācaritatvāt tu nipuṇān nāvabudhyase
english: Such inauspicious and dreadful customs as these, O Jājali, you do not, for all your skill, perceive, simply because they are universally practiced.

sanskrit: kāraṇād dharmam anvicchen na lokacaritaṃ caret yo hanyād yaś ca māṃ stauti tatrāpi śṛṇu jājale
english: One should seek dharma upon principle, and not merely follow the way of the world. As for him who would strike me and him who praises me—hear of this too, O Jājali:

sanskrit: samau tāv api me syātāṃ na hi me staḥ priyāpriye etad īdṛśakaṃ dharmaṃ praśaṃsanti manīṣiṇaḥ
english: those two would be alike to me, for I have neither liked nor disliked. Such a dharma as this the wise extol.

sanskrit: upapattyā hi saṃpanno yatibhiś caiva sevyate satataṃ dharmaśīlaiś ca naipuṇyenopalakṣitaḥ
english: For, furnished with sound reasoning, it is honored by ascetics and by those ever devoted to dharma, and it is marked out by its subtlety.

sanskrit: jājalir uvāca yathā pravartito dharmas tulāṃ dhārayatā tvayā svargadvāraṃ ca vṛttiṃ ca bhūtānām avarotsyate
english: Jājali said: By the dharma you have set forth, you who hold the scale, the gate of heaven and the very livelihood of creatures will be barred.

sanskrit: kṛṣyā hy annaṃ prabhavati tatas tvam api jīvasi paśubhiś cauṣadhībhiś ca martyā jīvanti vāṇija
english: For from agriculture food arises, and thereby you yourself live; and by cattle and by herbs do mortals live, O trader.

sanskrit: yato yajñaḥ prabhavati nāstikyam api jalpasi na hi varted ayaṃ loko vārtām utsṛjya kevalam
english: From these too sacrifice arises—yet you prate of the denier's creed; for this world could never go on if it abandoned husbandry altogether.

sanskrit: tulādhāra uvāca vakṣyāmi jājale vṛttiṃ nāsmi brāhmaṇa nāstikaḥ na ca yajñaṃ vinindāmi yajñavit tu sudurlabhaḥ
english: Tulādhāra said: I shall expound the right way of life, O Jājali; I am no denier, O brāhmaṇa, nor do I condemn sacrifice—yet one who truly knows sacrifice is very hard to find.

sanskrit: namo brāhmaṇayajñāya ye ca yajñavido janāḥ svayajñaṃ brāhmaṇā hitvā kṣātraṃ yajñam ihāsthitāḥ
english: Homage to the brāhmaṇa's sacrifice and to those who know sacrifice; for the brāhmaṇas have forsaken their own sacrifice and taken up here the kṣatriya's sacrifice.

sanskrit: lubdhair vittaparair brahman nāstikaiḥ saṃpravartitam vedavādān avijñāya satyābhāsam ivānṛtam
english: It has been set in motion, O brāhmaṇa, by the greedy, by those bent on wealth, by deniers who, not understanding the words of the Veda, take what is false for what merely wears the semblance of truth.

sanskrit: idaṃ deyam idaṃ deyam iti nāntaṃ cikīrṣati ataḥ stainyaṃ prabhavati vikarmāṇi ca jājale tad eva sukṛtaṃ havyaṃ yena tuṣyanti devatāḥ
english: 'This must be given, this must be given'—and he seeks no end to it; hence arise theft and forbidden deeds, O Jājali. That oblation alone is well made by which the gods are gladdened.

sanskrit: namaskāreṇa haviṣā svādhyāyair auṣadhais tathā pūjā syād devatānāṃ hi yathā śāstranidarśanam
english: By reverence, by oblation, by recitation of the Veda, and by herbs let the worship of the gods be performed, as the scriptures show.

sanskrit: iṣṭāpūrtād asādhūnāṃ viṣamā jāyate prajā lubdhebhyo jāyate lubdhaḥ samebhyo jāyate samaḥ
english: From the rites and works of the wicked is born a crooked offspring; from the greedy is born the greedy, from the impartial the impartial.

sanskrit: yajamāno yathātmānam ṛtvijaś ca tathā prajāḥ yajñāt prajā prabhavati nabhaso 'mbha ivāmalam
english: As is the sacrificer in himself, so too are his priests, and so his offspring; from sacrifice offspring arises, as pure water from the sky.

sanskrit: agnau prāstāhutir brahmann ādityam upatiṣṭhati ādityāj jāyate vṛṣṭir vṛṣṭer annaṃ tataḥ prajāḥ
english: The oblation cast into the fire, O brāhmaṇa, attends upon the sun; from the sun is born rain, from rain food, and from food creatures.

sanskrit: tasmāt svanuṣṭhitāt pūrve sarvān kāmāṃś ca lebhire akṛṣṭapacyā pṛthivī āśīrbhir vīrudho 'bhavan na te yajñeṣv ātmasu vā phalaṃ paśyanti kiṃ cana
english: Therefore, from sacrifice well performed, the men of old won all their desires; the earth ripened her harvests untilled, and the plants grew at their blessings—yet they looked for no reward in their sacrifices or in themselves at all.

sanskrit: śaṅkamānāḥ phalaṃ yajñe ye yajeran kathaṃ cana jāyante 'sādhavo dhūrtā lubdhā vittaprayojanāḥ
english: But those who, anxious for reward, would sacrifice in any selfish fashion are born again as wicked men, as cheats, as the greedy whose end is gain.

sanskrit: sa sma pāpakṛtāṃ lokān gacched aśubhakarmaṇā pramāṇam apramāṇena yaḥ kuryād aśubhaṃ naraḥ pāpātmā so 'kṛtaprajñaḥ sadaiveha dvijottama
english: By his unholy deeds such a one goes to the worlds of the doers of evil. The man who would make right out of wrong and do the unholy is of evil soul, of undeveloped wisdom, ever so here, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: kartavyam iti kartavyaṃ vetti yo brāhmaṇobhayam brahmaiva vartate loke naiti kartavyatāṃ punaḥ
english: The brāhmaṇa who knows both kinds of duty—what is to be done as that which is to be done—dwells as Brahman itself in the world, and falls back no more into the bondage of obligation.

sanskrit: viguṇaṃ ca punaḥ karma jyāya ity anuśuśruma sarvabhūtopaghātaś ca phalabhāve ca saṃyamaḥ
english: And action shorn of its qualities is the higher, so we have heard; that is, to forbear from harming any being, and to be restrained as to its fruit.

sanskrit: satyayajñā damayajñā alubdhāś cātmatṛptayaḥ utpannatyāginaḥ sarve janā āsannamatsarāḥ
english: Those whose sacrifice is truth, whose sacrifice is self-restraint, who are free of greed and content within themselves, renouncers of whatever arises—all such folk have set envy at a distance.

sanskrit: kṣetrakṣetrajñatattvajñāḥ svayajñapariniṣṭhitāḥ brāhmaṃ vedam adhīyantas toṣayanty amarān api
english: Knowing the truth of the field and the knower of the field, perfected in their own sacrifice, studying the holy Veda, they gladden even the immortals.

sanskrit: akhilaṃ daivataṃ sarvaṃ brahma brāhmaṇasaṃśritam tṛpyanti tṛpyato devās tṛptās tṛptasya jājale
english: All divinity entire, all Brahman, rests upon the brāhmaṇa; when he is satisfied the gods are satisfied, and they are content when the contented man is content, O Jājali.

sanskrit: yathā sarvarasais tṛpto nābhinandati kiṃ cana tathā prajñānatṛptasya nityaṃ tṛptiḥ sukhodayā
english: As one sated with every flavor takes joy in nothing more, so for him who is content in wisdom there is a contentment, perpetual, that gives rise to bliss.

sanskrit: dharmārāmā dharmasukhāḥ kṛtsnavyavasitās tathā asti nas tattvato bhūya iti prajñāgaveṣiṇaḥ
english: Delighting in dharma, finding their joy in dharma, wholly resolved, the seekers after wisdom say: 'There is yet more for us, beyond, in very truth.'

sanskrit: jñānavijñāninaḥ ke cit paraṃ pāraṃ titīrṣavaḥ atīva tat sadā puṇyaṃ puṇyābhijanasaṃhitam
english: Some, possessed of knowledge and discernment, longing to cross to the farthest shore beyond—that shore is supremely holy ever, joined with a holy lineage.

sanskrit: yatra gatvā na śocanti na cyavanti vyathanti ca te tu tad brahmaṇaḥ sthānaṃ prāpnuvantīha sāttvikāḥ
english: Going whither men neither grieve nor fall away nor suffer pain—those of pure nature attain here to that abode of Brahman.

sanskrit: naiva te svargam icchanti na yajanti yaśodhanaiḥ satāṃ vartmānuvartante yathābalam ahiṃsayā
english: They desire not heaven, nor do they sacrifice with wealth got for renown; they follow the path of the good, according to their power, through non-violence.

sanskrit: vanaspatīn oṣadhīś ca phalamūlaṃ ca te viduḥ na caitān ṛtvijo lubdhā yājayanti dhanārthinaḥ
english: Trees and herbs and fruit and root—these they know for their offerings; greedy priests, set on gain, do not conduct their sacrifices for them.

sanskrit: svam eva cārthaṃ kurvāṇā yajñaṃ cakruḥ punar dvijāḥ pariniṣṭhitakarmāṇaḥ prajānugrahakāmyayā
english: Pursuing only their own true purpose, the twice-born, perfected in their works, performed sacrifice once again, out of a wish to bless the people.

sanskrit: prāpayeyuḥ prajāḥ svargaṃ svadharmacaraṇena vai iti me vartate buddhiḥ samā sarvatra jājale
english: That they might lead the people to heaven by the practice of their own dharma—such is the conviction that abides in me, impartial in all things, O Jājali.

sanskrit: prayuñjate yāni yajñe sadā prājñā dvijarṣabha tena te devayānena pathā yānti mahāmune
english: By those rites which the wise ever employ in sacrifice, O bull among the twice-born, they journey along that path of the gods, O great sage.
